messages.content:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): leg_length, torso_mass, kd, leg_density, freq, knee_amp, kp, pitch_kp, hip_amp, balance_gain, foot_friction, ramp_s, torque_limit, foot_length
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): hip_bias, duty, fp_kv, fp_kd, stance_knee, sync_gain, start_lean, pitch_ref, knee_shift
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

MEMORY. Some messages list retrieved memory items (earlier episodes or mechanism cards, each with an id). They are hearsay from other robots, not facts about this robot. In your first reply assess EVERY retrieved item: applies, needs_adaptation, test_first (verify with an experiment before relying on it) or does_not_apply, with a reason. You may revise an assessment later.

PROTOCOL. One model call per step, at most 12 steps. Write the reply in the schema's order, which is the order of reasoning: (1) result_reading: what the newest measurements show physically (on the first step: what the initial observation shows), with numbers; (2) status_updates: a verdict for EVERY hypothesis that had predictions scored in the newest experiments (keep it open, mark it supported, refuted or unresolved, citing the experiment ids), and any other revision; (3) new_hypotheses, including new explanations when the evidence contradicts the current ones; (4) the action: ONE of counterfactual (one or two experiments), test (one stress test), repair (one or two repairs) or conclude, in the list of that name; the other action lists stay empty. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): leg_length, torso_mass, kd, leg_density, freq, knee_amp, kp, pitch_kp, hip_amp, balance_gain, foot_friction, ramp_s, torque_limit, foot_length
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): hip_bias, duty, fp_kv, fp_kd, stance_knee, sync_gain, start_lean, pitch_ref, knee_shift
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: tracking_error_knee, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation, flight_fraction, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, time_upright, slip_fraction, pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L, saturation_frac_knee, swing_clearance_min_over_L, com_vx_slope, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean, capture_inside_fraction, n_walking, pitch_rate_slope, angmom_norm_end, fall_time, pitch_slope, com_vx_end, saturation_frac_ankle, n_fell, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope, tracking_error_ankle, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, capture_margin_over_L_slope, step_length_over_L, angmom_norm_slope, com_height_over_L_end, friction_utilisation_p95, pitch_rate_mean, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, max_friction_utilisation, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, pre_fall.pitch, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, pre_fall.com_vx, capture_margin_over_L_end, step_freq_hz, com_height_over_L_slope, com_height_over_L_mean, pre_fall.angmom_norm, double_support_fraction, pitch_mean, com_vx_mean, tracking_error_hip, angmom_norm_mean, pitch_end, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, pre_fall.pitch_rate, pitch_rate_end, pre_fall.slip_fraction, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, capture_margin_over_L_mean, saturation_frac_hip. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

MEMORY. Some messages list retrieved memory items (earlier episodes or mechanism cards, each with an id). They are hearsay from other robots, not facts about this robot. In your first reply assess EVERY retrieved item: applies, needs_adaptation, test_first (verify with an experiment before relying on it) or does_not_apply, with a reason. You may revise an assessment later.

PROTOCOL. One model call per step, at most 12 steps. Write the reply in the schema's order, which is the order of reasoning: (1) result_reading: what the newest measurements show physically (on the first step: what the initial observation shows), with numbers; (2) status_updates: a verdict for EVERY hypothesis that had predictions scored in the newest experiments (keep it open, mark it supported, refuted or unresolved, citing the experiment ids), and any other revision; (3) new_hypotheses, including new explanations when the evidence contradicts the current ones; (4) the action: ONE of counterfactual (one or two experiments), test (one stress test), repair (one or two repairs) or conclude, in the list of that name; the other action lists stay empty. Reply with a single JSON object that follows the response schema; no prose.

Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02.

messages.content:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): freq, balance_gain, kp, knee_amp, ramp_s, pitch_kp, leg_length, kd, foot_length, foot_friction, hip_amp, torque_limit, torso_mass, leg_density
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): stance_knee, hip_bias, duty, fp_kd, knee_shift, pitch_ref, start_lean, fp_kv, sync_gain
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. policy_record.system_prompt:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): freq, balance_gain, kp, knee_amp, ramp_s, pitch_kp, leg_length, kd, foot_length, foot_friction, hip_amp, torque_limit, torso_mass, leg_density
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): stance_knee, hip_bias, duty, fp_kd, knee_shift, pitch_ref, start_lean, fp_kv, sync_gain
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): leg_length, foot_length, balance_gain, pitch_kp, torso_mass, torque_limit, kd, freq, knee_amp, leg_density, foot_friction, hip_amp, kp, ramp_s
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): duty, start_lean, knee_shift, pitch_ref, sync_gain, fp_kv, hip_bias, stance_knee, fp_kd
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.

Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. messages.content:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): leg_length, foot_length, balance_gain, pitch_kp, torso_mass, torque_limit, kd, freq, knee_amp, leg_density, foot_friction, hip_amp, kp, ramp_s
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): duty, start_lean, knee_shift, pitch_ref, sync_gain, fp_kv, hip_bias, stance_knee, fp_kd
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: pre_fall.pitch, time_upright, saturation_frac_hip, tracking_error_hip, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, angmom_norm_slope, step_freq_hz, max_friction_utilisation, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope, com_height_over_L_slope, pre_fall.slip_fraction, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, com_vx_mean, com_height_over_L_end, capture_inside_fraction, pre_fall.angmom_norm, pitch_rate_slope, pitch_rate_mean, pitch_slope, n_walking, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, com_height_over_L_mean, n_fell, friction_utilisation_p95, saturation_frac_ankle, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L, com_vx_slope, pitch_rate_end, pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, flight_fraction, capture_margin_over_L_slope, swing_clearance_min_over_L, com_vx_end, angmom_norm_end, angmom_norm_mean, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, step_length_over_L, tracking_error_ankle, pre_fall.pitch_rate, slip_fraction, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation, double_support_fraction, pre_fall.com_vx, pitch_end, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, saturation_frac_knee, capture_margin_over_L_mean, tracking_error_knee, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, fall_time, capture_margin_over_L_end, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, pitch_mean. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

MEMORY. Some messages list retrieved memory items (earlier episodes or mechanism cards, each with an id). They are hearsay from other robots, not facts about this robot. In your first reply assess EVERY retrieved item: applies, needs_adaptation, test_first (verify with an experiment before relying on it) or does_not_apply, with a reason. You may revise an assessment later.

PROTOCOL. One model call per step, at most 12 steps. Write the reply in the schema's order, which is the order of reasoning: (1) result_reading: what the newest measurements show physically (on the first step: what the initial observation shows), with numbers; (2) status_updates: a verdict for EVERY hypothesis that had predictions scored in the newest experiments (keep it open, mark it supported, refuted or unresolved, citing the experiment ids), and any other revision; (3) new_hypotheses, including new explanations when the evidence contradicts the current ones; (4) the action: ONE of counterfactual (one or two experiments), test (one stress test), repair (one or two repairs) or conclude, in the list of that name; the other action lists stay empty. Reply with a single JSON object that follows the response schema; no prose.

policy_record.system_prompt:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): leg_length, foot_length, balance_gain, pitch_kp, torso_mass, torque_limit, kd, freq, knee_amp, leg_density, foot_friction, hip_amp, kp, ramp_s
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): duty, start_lean, knee_shift, pitch_ref, sync_gain, fp_kv, hip_bias, stance_knee, fp_kd
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: pre_fall.pitch, time_upright, saturation_frac_hip, tracking_error_hip, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, angmom_norm_slope, step_freq_hz, max_friction_utilisation, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope, com_height_over_L_slope, pre_fall.slip_fraction, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, com_vx_mean, com_height_over_L_end, capture_inside_fraction, pre_fall.angmom_norm, pitch_rate_slope, pitch_rate_mean, pitch_slope, n_walking, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, com_height_over_L_mean, n_fell, friction_utilisation_p95, saturation_frac_ankle, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L, com_vx_slope, pitch_rate_end, pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, flight_fraction, capture_margin_over_L_slope, swing_clearance_min_over_L, com_vx_end, angmom_norm_end, angmom_norm_mean, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, step_length_over_L, tracking_error_ankle, pre_fall.pitch_rate, slip_fraction, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation, double_support_fraction, pre_fall.com_vx, pitch_end, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, saturation_frac_knee, capture_margin_over_L_mean, tracking_error_knee, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, fall_time, capture_margin_over_L_end, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, pitch_mean. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

MEMORY. Some messages list retrieved memory items (earlier episodes or mechanism cards, each with an id). They are hearsay from other robots, not facts about this robot. In your first reply assess EVERY retrieved item: applies, needs_adaptation, test_first (verify with an experiment before relying on it) or does_not_apply, with a reason. You may revise an assessment later.

PROTOCOL. One model call per step, at most 12 steps. Write the reply in the schema's order, which is the order of reasoning: (1) result_reading: what the newest measurements show physically (on the first step: what the initial observation shows), with numbers; (2) status_updates: a verdict for EVERY hypothesis that had predictions scored in the newest experiments (keep it open, mark it supported, refuted or unresolved, citing the experiment ids), and any other revision; (3) new_hypotheses, including new explanations when the evidence contradicts the current ones; (4) the action: ONE of counterfactual (one or two experiments), test (one stress test), repair (one or two repairs) or conclude, in the list of that name; the other action lists stay empty. Reply with a single JSON object that follows the response schema; no prose.
policy_record.tolerance: n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02.

prediction_accuracy.tolerance: n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02.
